_note_fetch_family: FETCH FAMILY POPULATION (Issue #301, POC-A2.1/2) — 26 cards the clause KIND already supported, authored as compendium ENTRIES rather than machinery. Every printed effect below was read off `tools/meta_tracker/cards.json` (the engine's own all_card_data dump), never memory. VOCABULARY ADDED HERE, on top of `_note_fetch`'s fields. Targets: `stage1` / `stage2` (the printed stage), `tera`, `pokemon_ex` (an ex-rule body: ex or Mega ex), `item` / `tool` / `stadium` (each a strict subset of the existing `trainer` class), `any` (a dig with no class restriction at all). Fields: `amount` = the printed cap on cards THIS clause may take, ABSENT MEANING ONE (so the three missing-amount fixes below stay bug-fixes instead of making an absent field ambiguous), with the explicit sentinel `"all"` for an unbounded 'any number of'. `choice` = true when the clause is ONE ALTERNATIVE of a single choice ('...or...', 'up to N in any combination of X and Y'): the card's true cap across its `choice` clauses is the MAX of their amounts, NEVER the sum — Max Rod takes 5 cards total, not 5 Pokemon AND 5 Energy. Absent means an independent leg whose amount ADDS (Dawn genuinely fetches a Basic AND a Stage 1 AND a Stage 2 = 3 cards). `dig_from` = `top` (default) | `bottom` (Dusk Ball looks at the BOTTOM 7). `name_family` = the printed NAME restriction, RECORDED VERBATIM AND UNDECIDED — `fetch_closure.fetch_target_matches` refuses such a clause for REACH rather than ignoring the field (ignoring it would read Hop's Bag as fetching any Basic), and the four carriers are ruled `partial` for exactly that (Issue #306 cross-post: `card_text.name_in_family` is the string half of the key, but the missing piece is a build-time index over the pool keyed by family; and note 1134's restriction is a SUBSTRING test, not the owner prefix the other three use, so one oracle cannot be assumed). Rider `discard_remainder` = the dug cards NOT taken go to the DISCARD (Explorer's Guidance) instead of being shuffled back. `trigger: on_attach` = the fetch fires when the card is ATTACHED from hand (Telepath Psychic Energy), joining on_evolve / on_bench_play / on_attack. NOTE `dest` absent means HAND — `_note_fetch` said 'deck (default)', which was a doc slip: no committed entry ever meant it and nothing reads the field. THE 26, each with its printed effect. 1125 Master Ball: a Pokemon -> hand. 1082 Hyper Aroma: up to 3 Stage 1 -> hand. 1115 Hop's Bag: up to 2 Basic Hop's Pokemon -> Bench. 1126 Precious Trolley: ANY NUMBER of Basics -> Bench. 1127 Tera Orb: a Tera Pokemon -> hand. 1132 Team Rocket's Great Ball: a Trainer -> hand. 1134 Team Rocket's Transceiver: a Supporter with 'Team Rocket' in its name -> hand. 1101 Call Bell: a Supporter -> hand, going-SECOND first turn only. 1109 Miracle Headset: up to 2 Supporters from DISCARD -> hand. 1205 Cyrano: up to 3 Pokemon {ex} -> hand. 1210 Brock's Scouting: up to 2 Basics OR 1 Evolution -> hand (two `choice` clauses). 1220 Team Rocket's Proton: up to 3 Basic Team Rocket's Pokemon -> hand. 1233 Canari: up to 4 {L} Pokemon -> hand, gated on discarding another card (`cost: discard_1`). 1077 Roto-Stick: top 4, any number of Supporters. 1094 Bug Catching Set: top 7, up to 2 in any combination of {G} Pokemon and Basic {G} Energy. 1102 Dusk Ball: BOTTOM 7, a Pokemon. 1185 Explorer's Guidance: top 6, take 2, DISCARD the rest. 1193 Hassel: top 8, up to 3, only if one of my Pokemon was KO'd during the opponent's last turn. 1231 Dawn: a Basic AND a Stage 1 AND a Stage 2. 1092 Secret Box: an Item AND a Tool AND a Supporter AND a Stadium, gated on discarding 3 (`cost: discard_3`). 1194 Colress's Tenacity: a Stadium AND an Energy. 1215 Ethan's Adventure: up to 3 in any combination of Ethan's Pokemon and Basic {R} Energy. 1238 Tarragon: up to 4 in any combination of {F} Pokemon and Basic {F} Energy, from DISCARD. 1184 Lana's Aid: up to 3 in any combination of no-Rule-Box Pokemon and Basic Energy, from DISCARD. 19 Telepath Psychic Energy (Special): provides {P}, and ON ATTACH to a {P} Pokemon searches for up to 2 Basic {P} Pokemon -> Bench. It carries TWO type gates and they are different questions: `energy_type: 5` is what may be FETCHED (Basic {P} Pokemon) and `target_type: 5` is the {P} RECIPIENT the attach must be made to for the fetch to fire at all — the same field name, and the same meaning, `accel` already uses for a restricted recipient (1146 Wondrous Patch), so this is one vocabulary rather than a second one. Without `target_type` the clause set would miss a printed restriction and the card would owe a `partial`. It is also the first card to carry BOTH kinds, so note the two spell a colour differently and deliberately: `energy_provide` names it as the string `type` (card 17 Ignition Energy's precedent, `_note_misc`) while `fetch` names its lock as the numeric EnergyType — each field belongs to its own kind's vocabulary, and unifying them is a change to card 17's committed clause, not to this entry. 1206 Larry's Skill: a Pokemon AND a Supporter AND a Basic Energy — authored, but `partial`: 'Discard your hand' is the card's whole cost and no clause field carries it (the 1192 precedent). ONE CARD IS DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED: 1188 Ciphermaniac's Codebreaking (4 copies, `slowking`) — 'search your deck for 2 cards ... then put those cards ON TOP of it'. `dest` has no such value and `deck_odds` has no notion of a KNOWN TOP, so it stays REFUSED and is cross-posted to Issue #289 (T3.5/11), which owns that concept; 4 copies in a shipped deck is the concrete reason that issue matters. It is one of the TWO fetch-family sites the census still reports; the other is 173 Noctowl's on-evolve Jewel Seeker Ability, which is outside this Trainer/Energy batch (0 copies, 0.00 meta). ON `covers` AND UNREAD FIELDS: a verdict is a statement about whether the CLAUSE SET describes the whole printed effect, NOT about whether a consumer reads every field of it — `amount` has no reader today (`combat._hand_yield_units` says so in as many words, and the reach graph asks only 'can this card find X at all'). So Buddy-Buddy Poffin is `full` because its clauses now say 'up to 2', and wiring a transition that spends that 2 is T4's job, not a reason to under-declare the data. That is the opposite of 1188, whose effect the vocabulary cannot express at all. _note_energy_recur: ENERGY_RECUR clauses (Issue #204) — the discard-reload PREDICATE the boolean `discard_energy_recur` Function Tag can't carry: how many, of what type, on WHAT TRIGGER, and to WHICH targets. The clock (`combat.turns_to_afford` via `discard_recur_fuel(scope='self_arming')`) needs all four to answer "does this reload pay for THIS body's own attack?"; the tag alone answers only "could they refuel at all", which is the fail-OPEN doom-relax caution and stays tag-routed. Probe-unreachable (neither effect resolves on a Trainer probe board) -> override-only, like the heal gates. Fields: amount = the printed cap; energy_type = the EnergyType code the reload is locked to; zone = where it comes FROM; trigger = on_evolve (an Ability firing as the evolution is played — the same hop the clock counts) | on_attack (an attack effect, which needs the body already armed); target = own_type | bench_only (whether the reloading body may take the Energy itself).
